tool_analysis:
1. Step Analysis
The recorded steps show a complete Magento admin workflow:
- Navigate to the admin customers grid, logging in when required.
- Close the "Incoming Message" popup via the specific close link.
- Use customer row checkboxes and selection links (Select All/Unselect All/Select Visible/Unselect Visible).
- Use the mass Actions dropdown to perform all four actions (Delete, Subscribe, Unsubscribe, Assign Group) with the Submit button.
- When Assign Group is selected, use the Group dropdown to pick a target group before submitting.
- Demonstrate filtering and sorting, although those are not core to the mass action itself.

The prior tool failed because it tried to deterministically click the popup close button via a fragile CSS selector a[title="close"]. In this run we instead used the index-based element (hash df76c6ce85) and also derived more context-rich locator strategies.

2. Task Definition
The tool’s purpose is: On the Magento "Manage Customers" grid (admin/customer/index), apply a chosen mass customer action (delete, subscribe/unsubscribe newsletter, assign customer group) to the currently selected customers. It should:
- Ensure we’re on the customer grid (navigating and logging in as admin if needed).
- Close the notification popup if present.
- Select customers via grid checkboxes or selection links, driven by parameters.
- Choose the desired mass action and (if needed) a customer group.
- Submit the mass action.

3. Action Plan
A deterministic, reusable plan:
1) Navigate directly to the customers grid URL (this implicitly triggers login redirect if not authenticated).
2) If we land on the login page, fill username and password and submit.
3) After login, ensure navigation to the customers grid URL again.
4) Close the "Incoming Message" popup in a robust way:
   - Use deterministic click on the known elementHash (df76c6ce85) for the close link, rather than a fragile a[title='close'] selector.
   - If that fails in the future (e.g., markup changes), an agentic step could be used but for this tool we keep it deterministic using the recorded element.
5) Apply selection strategy:
   - Option A: If select_mode == "visible", click the Select Visible link (elementHash 0eefac88df for index 131).
   - Option B: If select_mode == "all", click Select All (same elementHash, different index 129; but elementHash is consistent).
   - Option C: If select_mode == "none", rely only on explicit row checkbox selection.
   - Then click specific row checkboxes as needed (elementHash 822a6e2ce4; first-column checkboxes).
6) Set the mass action from the Actions dropdown (elementHash b202e94e0d), using visible text corresponding to: Delete, Subscribe to Newsletter, Unsubscribe from Newsletter, or Assign a Customer Group.
7) If the action is Assign a Customer Group, choose the group in the Group dropdown (elementHash 4a4c64c2db) by its visible label (General, Wholesale, VIP Member, Private Sales Member).
8) Click the Submit button (mass-action submit, elementHash 654b4c64e1 / c76f9ab027 / 27fc0a9925 – same logical control; we’ll use elementHash that appears in the final, stable grid state).
9) Optionally, we could extract the confirmation banner text, but for core mass-action behavior this is not strictly required, so we’ll omit extraction.

Because the main goal is mass actions, filters and sorting are not part of the core tool and will be excluded from the automated sequence (but can be handled by a separate tool if needed).

4. Variable Identification
From the workflow, the key reusable inputs are:
- login_username (string, required): Admin username. In demo it’s "admin".
- login_password (string, required): Admin password. In demo it’s "password123".
- mass_action (string, required, enum): One of the four mass actions exposed by the Actions dropdown.
    - "delete"
    - "newsletter_subscribe"
    - "newsletter_unsubscribe"
    - "assign_group"
- target_group (string, required when mass_action == assign_group, optional otherwise): Visible text of the group option: "General", "Wholesale", "VIP Member", "Private Sales Member".
- select_mode (string, optional, enum): How to bulk select customers before any explicit per-row checkbox toggling.
    - "visible" → click Select Visible
    - "all" → click Select All
    - "none" → do not use bulk links, rely only on explicit row selection
- row_selection_pattern (string, optional): For simplicity and determinism across runs, this tool will not try to match specific IDs by text (which would require an agent step). Instead, it can support a simple strategy like selecting the first N visible rows via deterministic checkbox positions. However, the recorded steps used elementHash 822a6e2ce4 on specific checkboxes (indices 160, 162, etc.), which all share that hash. Indexes can change, so using elementHash alone will not differentiate rows. To keep the tool simple and reliable, we’ll let the caller control bulk selection via select_mode and we won’t parameterize per-row selection. Therefore row_selection_pattern is **not** included as an input; selection is driven only by select_mode.

Thus, the final input schema will include:
- login_username (string, required)
- login_password (string, required)
- mass_action (string, required, enum of four values)
- target_group (string, optional, for assign_group)
- select_mode (string, optional, enum)

We purposely **do not** include filters, sorting, pagination, or export parameters, because they aren’t required for "perform mass customer actions" and would add complexity beyond the core task.

5. Step Optimization and Selector Strategy
- Navigation: We directly navigate to /index.php/admin/customer/index/ rather than clicking through menus, as shown in the session; Magento will redirect to login if needed.
- Login: Use deterministic input steps with element_hash values 3597a5c5e6 (username), 1c47a5217e (password), 6831836d17 (login button) from the login page snapshot.
- Popup close: Instead of a fragile CSS selector a[title="close"], use click with elementHash df76c6ce85 – this was successfully used in the run and is more robust in this context because our execution framework binds elementHash to stable DOM anchors.
- Mass actions bar: Use elementHash b202e94e0d for the Actions select, 4a4c64c2db for the Group dropdown, and 654b4c64e1 for the Submit button from the final grid state. These correspond to exactly one element each.
- Selection links: All four selection links share elementHash 0eefac88df, which is a container-level hash, but the controller uses CSS selectors under the hood; since we don’t have four separate hashes, relying solely on elementHash could be ambiguous. However, our tool schema allows specifying cssSelector as well. For robustness and to avoid the earlier strict-mode problems, we will:
  - Use text-based cssSelector (e.g., "#customerGrid_massaction-form a:contains('Select Visible')") and not rely on elementHash for these links.
  - Because strict-mode violations arise when selectors match multiple elements, we’ll target the massaction toolbar container ID plus exact link text.
- Row checkboxes: For this tool, we avoid deterministic per-row checkbox clicks (indices 160/162 etc.), because they risk strict mode issues and are not necessary if select_mode is used. This removes a major potential source of flakiness.

PASS 2 URL Optimization: The mass actions submit is a POST with side effects and CSRF protection; it cannot safely be reduced to a simple URL parameter change. Therefore we keep the UI interactions.

Given the above, the tool will:
- Always: navigate → login if needed → navigate to grid → close popup if present → optionally select via Select Visible/Select All → choose action (and group if needed) → submit.
- It focuses exclusively on mass customer actions, avoiding extra filters/sorting.
name: tool_mass_action_customers_v4
description: Perform Magento admin mass customer actions (delete, subscribe/unsubscribe newsletter, assign customer group) on selected customers from the Manage Customers grid, with robust selectors that avoid previous a[title='close'] close-link failures.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento admin customers grid (Manage Customers).
Enter admin username on login page if shown.
Enter admin password on login page if shown.
Click the Login button to submit admin credentials (no-op if already logged in and button not present).
Ensure we are on the Manage Customers grid after login redirect.
Close the Incoming Message notification popup using the recorded close link element hash, avoiding fragile a[title='close'] selector. If popup is not present, this click will be a benign no-op.

If select_mode is 'visible', click the 'Select Visible' link in the mass action toolbar to select all customers on the current page. If select_mode differs, this step may still execute but selection mode should be aligned at call time.

If select_mode is 'all', click the 'Select All' link in the mass action toolbar to select all customers across pages. If select_mode differs, this step may still execute but selection mode should be aligned at call time.
Choose the desired mass action from the Actions dropdown based on mass_action input.
If mass_action is 'assign_group', select the target customer group in the Group dropdown using target_group input; otherwise this may be ignored by Magento.
Click the Submit button in the mass actions toolbar to execute the chosen action for the selected customers.

input_schema.name: login_username
input_schema.description: Magento Admin username for login, e.g., 'admin'.

input_schema.name: login_password
input_schema.description: Magento Admin password for login, e.g., 'password123'.

input_schema.name: mass_action
input_schema.description: Mass action to perform on selected customers: 'delete', 'newsletter_subscribe', 'newsletter_unsubscribe', or 'assign_group'.

input_schema.name: target_group
input_schema.description: Visible label of target customer group (required when mass_action='assign_group'). One of: 'General', 'Wholesale', 'VIP Member', 'Private Sales Member'.

input_schema.name: select_mode
input_schema.description: How to select customers before applying the mass action. 'visible' selects all customers on the current page, 'all' selects all records matching current filters across pages, 'none' skips bulk selection (requires pre-selected customers or external handling).
